concepts.def: Exchanges energy and matter with surroundings; coasts gain sediment, lose energy.
Energy (waves, wind, tides) and matter (sediment from rivers, cliffs).
Erosion, transport, deposition processes operating within the system.
Energy dissipation, sediment exported to offshore sinks.
Balance of sediment inputs and outputs within a coastal cell.
Self-regulating coast adjusts form to balance inputs and outputs.

walkthroughs.body_html: Wave energy varies with fetch: Atlantic waves on western UK coasts have fetch of 5000+ km producing high-energy environments. Sediment inputs include rivers (UK rivers deliver ~10 million tonnes/yr), cliff erosion (Holderness ~1.8 m/yr retreat) and offshore sources.

DRARP framework: Destructive waves erode; Refraction concentrates energy on headlands; Attrition reduces clast size; Rotation moves sediment seasonally; Plunging breakers undermine cliffs. Longshore drift transports along coast at zigzag angle.

Sediment outputs include offshore loss to deep water, aeolian transport inland and human extraction. When inputs equal outputs, the coast is in dynamic equilibrium. Disruption (e.g. dam building reducing river load) triggers adjustment.
